name: arc-divider-copy-motif
description: Use when ARC grids contain divider lines separating repeated compartments. Copy a populated motif across matching blank cells.
---

# ARC divider-separated motif copying

Use this when a grid has one or more full-length, uniform divider lines separating compartments, with a structured motif in one compartment and corresponding blank compartments.

1. Identify the divider color and the compartments it creates. Treat the divider cells as boundaries, not motif cells.
2. Compare compartment dimensions. Equal-sized compartments strongly suggest direct translation; horizontal and vertical dividers can create a 2D array of matching cells.
3. Locate the compartment containing the motif. Distinguish its background color from its foreground marks, and include all cells in the motif's footprint—including background-colored cells and zeros—so the copied shape is exact.
4. Copy the entire compartment cell-for-cell into each matching blank compartment using the same row/column offsets. Preserve every color and leave divider lines unchanged.
5. Before submitting, verify grid dimensions, divider positions, and that each filled compartment is an exact translated copy. If compartments do not match in size or multiple plausible motifs exist, request another demonstration rather than guessing.

## Observed example

An 11x11 grid with a uniform color-4 row and column through the center creates four 5x5 compartments around the divider. The top-left compartment contains the motif; duplicating it unchanged into the other three compartments solves the pattern. A separate demonstration used color-7 vertical dividers and copied a 4-column motif region horizontally into the matching compartments. The shared rule is exact motif replication across equal-sized divider-separated regions.",
